title: Mueller-Hinton Agar

references.label: Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) Performance Standards for Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing

purpose: The standardized medium used for disk diffusion and other antimicrobial susceptibility testing methods, chosen for its consistent, low levels of certain inhibitors and good diffusion characteristics.
targetOrganisms: Non-fastidious organisms undergoing antimicrobial susceptibility testing; fastidious organisms typically require a supplemented or alternative CLSI-specified medium

reference.label: Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) Performance Standards for Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing

finalPh.value: CLSI specifies a target pH range appropriate for susceptibility testing; verify the exact current value in the edition being followed
finalPh.dependsOn: the specific CLSI document edition in use

preparationSummary: Prepare per manufacturer/CLSI instructions; agar depth in the plate is standardized (CLSI specifies an approximate depth) because it affects diffusion and therefore zone size interpretation.

sterilization.value: commonly autoclaved at 121°C for the time specified by the manufacturer/CLSI for the batch size
sterilization.dependsOn: batch size and the specific CLSI edition/manufacturer instructions in use

storage: Store per manufacturer guidance, protected from contamination and excessive drying, since drying changes effective agar depth/diffusion.
expectedAppearance: Pale, translucent to slightly opaque agar, poured to a standardized depth.
qualityControl: CLSI specifies routine QC using reference control organism strains and expected zone-diameter ranges — do not substitute an uncontrolled batch for susceptibility reporting.
manufacturerNotes: Because this medium underpins clinical susceptibility interpretation, always follow the current CLSI document edition rather than a remembered or older specification — breakpoints and QC ranges are revised periodically.
